title: Quickstart landing: interactive sandbox hero and progressive step diagram
text:
Quickstart landing: interactive sandbox hero and progressive step diagram

description:
Goal: Refresh the Quickstart landing hero to ship a lightweight, interactive 'live sandbox' that lets new users run a sample Redwood API call in-place, paired with a progressive step diagram that visually guides first-time flows. This ticket covers designs, annotated specs, responsive screenshot variants, and final art assets for engineering handoff.

Primary objectives:
- Design an accessible hero with an embedded single-step sandbox (code snippet + Run button) that simulates a request against a demo model and streams output. The sandbox must degrade to a static screenshot/faux-output in low-bandwidth or when embedding is blocked.
- Create a progressive step diagram (3 phases: Connect, Try, Iterate) that uses minimal animation to demonstrate state transitions and features the updated iconography and motion tokens. Diagram must be export-friendly as SVG/PNG and have a text-only fallback for docs.
- Produce screenshot variants (desktop/tablet/mobile and low-bandwidth static) and a naming convention for asset pipeline (qs_hero_desktop_v1.png, qs_hero_mobile_static_v1.jpg, etc.). Provide a script-friendly checklist for automated capture (viewport sizes, simulated network throttling, token-masking).
- Ship copy/CTA variants for A/B testing: "Try sandbox" (primary) vs "Run a demo" (secondary). Provide recommended analytics hooks (cta_click, sandbox_run_attempt, sandbox_run_success).

Acceptance criteria:
- Figma file with annotated hero & diagram frames and exportable assets.
- Accessibility notes: keyboard focus states, ARIA labels for interactive elements, reduced-motion variant.
- Engineering constraints called out: iframe height/width breakpoints, CORS fallback behavior, content-security-policy notes, and recommended mock API responses for deterministic screenshots.
- QA checklist and handoff doc in Confluence with links to GitHub PR for asset import.

Constraints & trade-offs considered:
- Live iframe vs client-side simulated runner: live iframe provides realistic demo but increases CSP/CORS complexity and privacy risk. We recommend a simulated client-runner for hosted Quickstart (vanilla JS that hits a Redwood demo proxy endpoint) and an iframe fallback only if engineering can guarantee the proxy origin.
- Animations: keep motion minimal (opacity/translate) to avoid distracting developers and to ensure good perf on low-end devices. Provide a reduced-motion variant.
- Image fidelity vs file size: provide SVG for diagrams and 3 PNG/JPEG sizes for hero screenshots; low-bandwidth variant uses compressed JPEG with alt text indicating simplified content.

Deliverables:
- Figma master screens (hero interactive states, progressive diagram states, responsive layouts).
- Exported assets folder with naming convention and three viewport variants.
- Confluence handoff doc: implementation notes, accessibility checklist, and QA script.
- PR template with asset import and screenshot links.


comments:
2025-11-05 - Kickoff (Ava C): Met with PM (Jordan) and Eng leads (Riya, Omar). Agreed scope: single-step sandbox only for initial launch, progressive diagram to be static SVG with micro-animations. Action: produce high-fidelity desktop + mobile hero by 11/18.
2025-11-12 - Wireframes posted to Figma (Ava C): Early frames shared. Engineering note from Riya: avoid cross-origin iframe where possible; propose mock-runner using demo proxy. Marking for accessibility review next week.
2025-11-18 - Design review (Team): Feedback: Increase contrast on CTA; simplify code snippet to 2 lines; provide keyboard focus for Run button. PM Jordan asks we prepare two CTA copy variants for A/B test. Assigned to Marco for visual polish.
2025-11-22 - Accessibility review (Nadia): Request: Add ARIA-live region for streaming output, provide reduced-motion states, include alt text for every exported image. Added to acceptance criteria.
2025-11-27 - Engineering sync (Omar): Confirmed mock-runner approach and agreed API for deterministic mock responses. Raised security question: demo proxy access logging and rate-limiting. Action: PM to confirm logging policy with Security.
2025-12-01 - First export (Marco R): Uploaded initial asset set to Drive. Files: qs_hero_desktop_v1.png, qs_hero_mobile_v1.png, qs_diagram_v1.svg. Link in attachments. Noted: mobile screenshot needs tighter cropping around code snippet.
2025-12-03 - PM feedback (Jordan): Prefer 'Try sandbox' as primary CTA for experiments. Add analytics hooks for sandbox_run_attempt and sandbox_run_success; reference analytics spec doc.
2025-12-06 - Design QA pass (Ava): Verified reduced-motion frames and keyboard flows in Figma prototypes. Minor update: change Run button focus ring to 3px according to design tokens. Ready for handoff.
2025-12-08 - PR opened (Marco): GitHub PR #8742 created to add assets and update landing markup prototype. Awaiting Eng review and security confirmation for demo proxy. Link in attachments.
2025-12-09 - In-review note (Ava): Incorporating engineering feedback from Riya on safe embedding. Added fallback static screenshot + 'Open sandbox' full-screen modal pattern for blocked embeds. Please review before closing.
Follow-ups after launch: schedule A/B metrics review at 2 weeks post-launch to compare CTA performance and sandbox engagement rates.
